ladder: The assay office kept the town's gold, so the town kept the office locked. Locks outlive their keyholders.
Where does a town that buried half its men keep the key to the room that mattered? Somewhere honest. Somewhere it goes to remember them.
The key hangs beneath the memorial board in the chapel. Take it, unlock the door with the key, open the door, and search the bench inside.
The storekeeper recommends the canary, and he is not making conversation.
Miners carried birds below because the birds knew things first. What killed miners in the Hollowdeep was not always the air.
Take the canary from the general store — it is on credit — and carry the cage on every trip below the workings. While you hold it, the thing that walks the cavern keeps its distance.
The timekeeper kept the wages, and the nook is barely a step off the junction. Nobody ever collected.
The winze is full of black water, and keeping it out used to be somebody's whole job.
The great pump in the pump room is missing exactly one argument, and the stables are where handles go to be mended.
Take the pump handle from the stables to the pump room. Use the pump once to seat the handle, then use it again to drain the winze.
The miners left the garnets and kept the roof up. That was not indecision. It was a priced decision.
The stull will come out if you pull it. What happens next happens on a schedule, and the schedule is short.
Pull the stull, take the garnets, and be out of the gallery within six moves. If the roof wins the race, the garnets keep — search the rubble afterward.
The foreman kept his effects, and nobody in ninety years has asked him for them.
He was a big man in good boots, and his pockets were part of his office.
Search the foreman. Take the watch, and read the tally book he carried — words written twice and underlined repay attention.
The foreman signed for everything, including the things that go bang.
Offices keep their secrets in furniture. His desk has a drawer with opinions.
Search the desk in the foreman's office. The magazine key is pushed to the back of the drawer.
The old men had working words, and the cave has heard them all. It remembers the useful ones.
One of them is scratched at waist height on a timber in the long drift, plain as a signature — with a note about where it works.
Read the scratched stull in the long drift, then say what it says while standing at the shaft head or the shaft foot.
The last lousy point is real, and it is somewhere the assay ledger never went.
The foreman's tally book records one word twice, underlined hard enough to tear the paper. Words like that are addresses.
Read the tally book, stand in the broken drift, and say the underlined word.
The passages are alike because nobody down there was decorating. Your own possessions, however, are not alike.
Drop something in a room and that room stops being every room. And somewhere in the maze, the air refuses to keep still.
Mark rooms with dropped items until the maze admits its shape. One room has a draught from the east — east from there is the breach. The dead end holds a cache worth the detour.
The seam in the gallery of veils is worth more than the mine ever shipped. It is also, at present, part of the wall.
Freeing it is a question of leverage — and of what the noise will wake.
Use the steel gad on the seam. The crack will carry a long way. Be holding the canary's cage before you swing.
The pearls sit behind a rim the water spent ages building, and the water is still on duty.
Taking them starts an argument you cannot win by standing in the room.
Take the pearls and leave the gour pools at once. You have about five moves before the water takes the room back.
The gleam in the pothole has outlasted a century of the river's own pulling. Your fingers are not news to it.
What shifts wedged things is steel and leverage, and the mine left plenty of both lying about.
Use the steel gad on the pothole.
The wall at the end of the maze was mortared from the far side. Nobody builds like that to keep people out.
The mine kept powder for exactly this argument, and safety fuse for having it from a distance.
Carry the keg and the fuse coil to the breach. Use the keg, then use the fuse, then light the fuse. Do not light the keg. The label agrees.
The plates are a library, and libraries reward browsing.
One plate is not like the others, and it is not on top.
Search the stacks in the tally chamber, then read what you find.
The mechanism is not locked. It is particular.
It wants a hand that carries its weight differently than yours does — or something made by one.
Use the bronze tool from the toolroom on the mechanism. If you already banked the tool, fetch it back — the office lends against deposits.
